text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 3.2% today as crude oil prices dropped more than 7% on Monday following news of potential U.S.-Iran peace talks. When oil prices fall, refiners like Marathon face lower margins on the fuel they produce and sell—their profit depends partly on the spread between what they pay for crude and what they receive for gasoline and diesel. The stock had already declined 9% over the prior two weeks, signaling investor concern even before today's oil selloff.

The timing adds pressure: Marathon announced a leadership change and company update on October 29th, just as analysts were flagging that Big Oil earnings guidance—not just reported profits—would be what investors scrutinize most closely going forward. With crude now down sharply and refineries running at 92.8% capacity (a fairly healthy level), any further softening in oil prices could constrain the refinery margins that drive Marathon's returns.
